newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals sees fall in SARB oversold rand forward book.
newsitem.headline: Stals sees fall in SARB oversold rand forward book.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank's oversold forward foreign exchange book could decline sharply in 1997, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday.
Stals said in an interview that the net oversold foreign exchange position of the central bank had fallen from $28 billion in 1995 to just $8 billion in February 1996.
It then rose sharply as South Africans rushed for cover in the wake of the collapse of the rand. Stals said last month it stood at that time at around $20 billion.
But just as the oversold position had climbed rapidly in 1996, so it was likely to decline in 1997 as South Africans decided the rand was steadying, he said.

"To take out forward cover is quite a costly operation, so many importers and South African residents with foreign commitments will gradually start to reconsider the risk of taking out forward cover and that forward book can then decline very sharply and very quickly," he said.
"Assuming events do not overtake us again, we will then be able to make very important permanent changes to the forward market."
